evidence.claim: Goose Lake has carried a ferry and has also dried out completely.
evidence.quote: The lake completely dried up in the years 1851, 1852, 1926, 1929–1934, 1992, 2009, and 2013–2015.

evidence.claim: During high water, at least from 1908 to 1912, the ferry Lakeview carried passengers and cargo between Davis Creek and Lakeview.
evidence.quote: During Goose Lake's high-water years, at least from 1908 to 1912, Davis Creek served as the southern port on the lake to and from which the ferry, Lakeview carried passengers and cargo for the town of Lakeview, Oregon at the north end of the lake.

evidence.claim: The railway reached Davis Creek in 1911; the port fell out of use as lake levels dropped and the railroad continued to Lakeview.
evidence.quote: The Nevada-California-Oregon Railway from Reno reached Davis Creek in 1911. The port fell into disuse as lake waters receded and the railroad was completed to Lakeview.

evidence.claim: This alkaline lake crosses the Oregon-California border.
evidence.quote: Goose Lake is a large alkaline lake in the Goose Lake Valley on the Oregon–California border in the United States.

evidence.claim: Its recorded dry periods include 1851 and 2013 through 2015, so a lake on the map does not establish present water conditions.
